clue.text: Creative types who may become rigid, leading to grouse

definitions.text: who may become rigid, leading to grouse

blocks.note: first meaning: the people who compose crosswords

blocks.clueFragment: who may become rigid, leading to grouse
blocks.note: second meaning: gun dogs that freeze stiffly to point out game birds for the shooters

explanation.surface: Artists who stiffen up and end up complaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grouse' looks like the verb for grumbling; it is the game bird. A setter is a hunting dog that stands rigid to show where birds are hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both crossword compilers, like Brendan himself, and a breed of hunting dog that 'sets' to indicate game.

clue.text: For changing pace endlessly, how like Brendan? Very playful

indicators.note: letters that are changing are being rearranged into a new order
without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
a lick is a speed, as in 'at a fair lick'
Brendan is the setter, so 'how like him' is the colloquial 'so me'

explanation.surface: The setter boasts that altering his pace is typical of his playful nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's so me' is slang for 'that's typical of me'; since Brendan is speaking, he is ME. FRO + LIC + SO ME gives FROLICSOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Frolicsome describes someone full of frolics, lively and fond of fun and games.

clue.text: Pros must cover this part of speech for 15 16, for instance

definitions.text: Pros must cover this part of speech for 15 16, for instance

blocks.clueFragment: Pros must cover this part of speech
blocks.note: surface reading: professionals have to deal with a grammar category
setter's reading: put the answer inside PROS and you get the word class of 'you', 'me' and 'us'

explanation.surface: Experts in grammar have to teach a particular word class.
explanation.walkthrough: Put PROS around the answer and it makes PRONOUNS, the part of speech that 15 16 (YOU, ME AND US) belongs to; the answer is itself a part of speech, a NOUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun is the word class naming people, places and things, and adding PRO in front gives the related category of stand-in words.

clue.text: Serves what solver wants

blocks.note: first meaning: does the job, as in 'that serves the purpose'
second meaning: the solutions a puzzler is hunting for

explanation.walkthrough: 'Serves' looks like a tennis or restaurant word; here it means suffices, as something that fits the bill does.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means satisfies a need; as a plural noun it means solutions, the reward every crossword solver is after.

clue.text: Passionately prepares to seek answer, going down

definitions.text: Passionately prepares to seek answer, going down

blocks.note: surface reading: a keen solver gearing up to crack a clue
setter's reading: a suitor about to propose drops on one leg to ask the big question; 'going down' also hints at a Down clue

explanation.surface: An eager puzzler gets ready to tackle a Down clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'answer' sought is a yes to a marriage proposal, and the passionate suitor kneels to ask it.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down on bended knee is the classic posture of someone proposing marriage, which is literally asking for an answer.

clue.text: Finishes off plum Araucaria crossword puzzle as constructed

indicators.note: the finishes of words are their final letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the last letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: Someone completes a choice puzzle by the legendary setter Araucaria exactly as it was built.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria was a much-loved Guardian setter, so the surface sounds like a solver's tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made has been constructed or built, so the past participle matches 'as constructed' in sense.

clue.text: Reminder from this compiler with short guide

indicators.note: something short is lacking its end, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the setter referring to himself
a mentor is a trusted guide

explanation.surface: A keepsake from the setter accompanied by a brief instruction leaflet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This compiler' is the standard way for a setter to clue ME.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake or souvenir kept to remind you of a person or event.

clue.text: You and I answer right one kind of clue, overcome by persistence

blocks.note: the pronoun for the two of us
A is the usual abbreviation for answer
R is the abbreviation for right
crossword clues are either Across or Down

explanation.surface: Setter and solver get one clue right, but only by dogged effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a solving session; the comma marks off the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To wear someone down is to beat their resistance gradually through relentless pressure.

clue.text: Great compiler’s brief self-introduction was astounding

definitions.note: a past-tense verb: 'it amazed people' means 'it was astounding to people'

indicators.note: a brief version has been shortened, so a letter is dropped from the phrase

blocks.note: how you introduce yourself: 'I am ...'; the shortening drops the I
Azed is the pseudonym of the Observer's famous barred-grid setter

explanation.surface: A famous setter's short opening remarks stunned the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The great compiler introduces himself as 'I am Azed'; clipped of its I it reads AM AZED, run together into one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb amazed, as in 'it amazed everyone', describes something that was astonishing to those who saw it.

clue.text: Anagram isn’t well assimilated? Not fully as yet

indicators.note: the setter simply names the device outright, telling us to rearrange what follows

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A solver has not really got the hang of a particular jumbled-letter clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagram' looks like the subject of the sentence but is the instruction itself; the definition then runs across the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something still new has not yet become familiar, so it has not been fully absorbed or taken in.

clue.text: What’s prior to this contribution from Ximenes (before 1000)

definitions.text: What’s prior to this contribution from Ximenes (before 1000)

blocks.note: surface reading: something coming before; in the grid this clue's number comes just before 12
setter's reading: the letters of XIMENES that come before M, the Roman thousand, are XI, a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A puzzle by the old master Ximenes, dated to before the year 1000.
explanation.walkthrough: Ximenes was a celebrated Observer setter. Split his name at M (1000) and the front part, XI, is a Roman number; this entry is also numbered as the one just before 12.
explanation.definitionFit: XI is the Roman numeral for the number after ten, and that number is also the one immediately preceding twelve.

clue.text: Scrub verticals I wrecked – they’re in column on left

indicators.note: something wrecked is smashed up, so its letters end up scattered and rebuilt

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cancels the Down clues in disgust, and the people involved are lined up on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the grid: the leftmost column holds 1 Down SETTERS and 17 Down SOLVERS, both kinds of crossword enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword setters and solvers are all lovers of puzzles, and the two entries in the grid's first column are exactly those people.

clue.text: Beginnings of brutal misdirection, a trap I’ve contrived for sucker

indicators.note: the beginnings of words are their opening letters, so only those are taken
something contrived is artificially devised, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of each word
taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A harsh setter devises a trick to catch a gullible solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' looks like a dupe who falls for the trap; it is a creature that sucks blood.
explanation.definitionFit: This bat feeds by drinking the blood of animals, so it is literally a blood-sucking creature.

clue.text: Put together halves of fair clue, yet had awfully regretful expression

indicators.note: taking only half of each word means the other half is thrown away
done awfully means badly done, so the letters come out in a muddle

blocks.note: the second half of the word
the second half of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter combines bits of a decent clue and regrets the clumsy result.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves taken are the back halves, IR from fair and UE from clue; the front halves are discarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you rue the day is an idiom of remorse, wishing something had never happened.

clue.text: 12, separately, then together, as expression of our relationship

blocks.note: setter's reading: the crossword folk taken one by one are the solver and the setter, and the two together
surface reading: a phrase for the bond between two people

explanation.surface: Puzzle lovers describe their bond first individually and then as a pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is CRUCIVERBALISTS: the setter addresses the solver as the second person, calls himself the first, and joins them in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase lists two people and then the pair, a common way of describing a partnership or couple.

clue.text: See 15
They provide solutions learner in second parts of test needed

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so a letter goes within a word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
L is the learner-driver plate
a Test is a cricket international, played in overs of six balls each

explanation.surface: A student needs some solutions to get through the second half of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test' sounds like an exam; in crosswords it often means a Test match, an international cricket game, and its parts are overs.
explanation.definitionFit: Solvers work out answers, so they are the people who come up with the solutions to puzzles.

clue.text: Journey I can take – after solving hard puzzle really quickly?

definitions.text: Journey I can take – after solving hard puzzle really quickly?

blocks.note: setter's reading: a voyage of the self, since the Latin for I is the word for one's sense of self

blocks.clueFragment: after solving hard puzzle really quickly?
blocks.note: surface reading: the smug glow of a speedy finish

explanation.surface: A solver rewards themselves with a trip after cracking a tough crossword fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'journey' is not travel at all but the swagger of someone delighted with themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an episode of self-indulgent pride, exactly how a speedy solver of a hard puzzle might feel.

clue.text: With clue, err badly – like Torquemada, but more so

indicators.note: done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter goes wrong with a clue, out-torturing even the notorious Torquemada.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquemada was the head of the Spanish Inquisition and also the pen name of a famously fiendish Observer setter. The answer uses the American spelling with one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquemada is a byword for cruelty, so 'like him but more so' asks for the comparative of cruel.

clue.text: Explanations for other things posted, not revealing parts of solutions

blocks.note: first meaning: notes sent with a job application or parcel explaining the contents
second meaning: hiding some of the characters of an answer, as a cheat-proof hint might

explanation.surface: Someone posting puzzle solutions takes care not to give any of them away.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: hiding (covering) the characters (letters) of an answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering letter accompanies a document in the post to explain it, while covering letters literally conceals characters of a word.

clue.text: Develop modern car with interior from one who works on things like this

indicators.note: the interior of a word is everything except its outer letters

blocks.note: EV is an electric vehicle

blocks.clueFragment: one who works on things like this
blocks.note: someone who works on crosswords is a solver; its inside letters are kept

explanation.surface: A puzzler helps design a modern car from the inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Things like this' means crossword clues, so the person who works on them is a SOLVER, whose interior is OLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To evolve is to grow or change gradually into a more advanced form, which is what developing means.

clue.text: Clue for King Edward? Clue fair, but oddly characterless

indicators.note: without the odd characters only the even-numbered letters remain

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A setter asks for a clue for a variety of potato, but the result is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is a British potato variety, but here the answer fits both words: King Lear of Shakespeare and Edward Lear the nonsense poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to Shakespeare's tragic monarch and to Edward the Victorian writer of limericks.

clue.text: Ready to enter, like clues you like, including extremes of theme

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so the first and last letters are taken
to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: solvers put a tick against clues they enjoy
the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A solver's favourite clues fit the puzzle's theme and are ready to be filled in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready to enter' suggests writing an answer in the grid; it means holding a ticket for admission.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ticketed has a pass for an event, so they are permitted to go in.

clue.text: Article which includes this old-fashioned part of crossword

indicators.note: a phrase that includes something carries it within its run of letters

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word break

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature that contains an antique piece of a crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'artiCLE Which'. It is the archaic spelling of the word we use for a crossword hint.
explanation.definitionFit: An older spelling of the familiar word for a crossword hint, from the ball of thread that guided Theseus out of the labyrinth.

clue.text: Obscure stuff that’s partly unfamiliar can annoy

indicators.note: partly means only a portion, so the answer is a section of the words that follow

blocks.note: the run of letters across the word breaks

explanation.surface: Arcane material that is somewhat strange can be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles 'unfamiliAR CAN Annoy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcana are secrets or mysterious knowledge understood only by a few initiates.

clue.text: A setter I trashed keeps doing the same thing

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so its letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter whose puzzles get trashed by critics stubbornly repeats the same approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Keeps' might suggest a container, but nothing is held here; it is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to repeat a process again and again, so a verb in the third person matches the phrase.
